defects.defect: The daily Google sign-in check is not in wave A; it is the first build step of wave B. The approved simplification S14 adds that check with mail, and its card is there so that a dead sign-in does not first show up as a missing or empty morning text. Wave A therefore ends with two unattended 07:00 jobs that rest on stored sign-ins and nothing that reports a dead one, until wave B's first phase. That is not a state that is safe to leave running. The check needs only gog and one stored sign-in, both present on day one, so nothing forces it out of A except size.

By my count wave A is 25.25 h and 51 steps as drawn (card hours from the sizing file, one hour to get ready and a three-hour exit gate, as M1's own phases had, plus about half an hour for the T4 and seeded-mail runs of Jordan's lookup pair, which the sizing file does not count). That is a little over one plan, so a piece has to move, and what gives way is the wrong way round. The piece named first (the two paper cards, phase 4) is drawn inside the eight-day wait, so it is already done when an overrun shows in the reader, the 07:00 text, the second inbox or the lookup. The piece that then really goes is the lookup (phase 8, last), which Tony asked for in wave A, while the second inbox (phase 7), the one piece the wave rule allows only 'as far as it fits', is built before it.

Three plans in a row sit at or over the ceiling with no room: by my count A is 25.25 h and 51 steps, B 24.25 h and 49, C 24.25 h and 49. These are the plans that hold the untried tests T1 to T8 and a connector that is not installed yet. Wave B is full because it already carries the sign-in check from A, so whatever A passes on pushes the day out two waves further, to D. With the day out and the flyer dates D is 23.75 h; if C also sends its second piece (the evening text), D is 25.75 h and the chain runs on: the coverage planner to E (26 h), the clash watch to F (25 h), the group chat to G. It resolves, but only by moving a card in six waves.

The clash watch goes live without the two checks its card lists as untried: that the connector's conflict or free/busy command works on a calendar shared as busy-only under the read-only grant, and that a command job can use the stored calendar sign-in. The other two proposals put the first check in the go-live line.

Waves H and I are 14 h and 28 steps each by my count, under the floor of one plan (roughly 15 hours). Together they hold 20 card-hours and carry 8 hours of getting ready and exit gates. Both can be executed; the cost is two sign-offs for one plan's worth of work, bought to keep one kind of risk per wave.

Exit tests that stop short of the goal. Wave A: only Tony asks 'did I get an email about X?', although the goal says each parent can, and the T4 and seeded-mail runs for Jordan's pair (about half an hour) are not in the count. Wave C: only the planted flyer that must set nothing is run; no real flyer is turned into reminders after a yes. Waves E and F: the page watch, the clash watch and the weekly text are hand-started only, so no run is seen arriving by itself and the schedule lines (hours, time zone) are not proven the way they are in A and C.

Over one plan as drawn, by my count: 25.75 h and 51 steps against its own 25 h and 49. The difference is small and has two sources: getting ready is counted at 0.75 h in every wave where M1's Prepare phase was about one hour, and the T4 and seeded-mail runs for Jordan's lookup pair (about half an hour) are flagged in the basis but not counted. So Jordan's inbox does not fit in wave A beside the sign-in check; it should be drawn as the opening phase of wave B as the expected case, not as an exception. This proposal is the one where that works: her inbox is the last build phase of A, B is then about 24.25 h and 49 steps, and anything B passes on lands in D, which has room. What is missing is the form of A's exit test for that case; as written it needs both 07:00 texts live.

Test T8, the stop-and-check sheet and Jordan's half page come a full plan after the first unattended texts. From wave A's exit both parents get a daily 07:00 text with nothing on paper that says what it is, how Tony switches it off, or how Jordan can tell that Happy is down. The wave A that Tony saw held these cards. They need nothing from wave B.

T7 is in phase 6, the last build phase but one, after T5's scheduling-tool turn in phase 3. The sizing file puts T7 first, then T5 for the scheduling tool. A failed T7 removes about 6 hours of work (the reminder rule, the recipient test, the grant, flyer dates) and takes project check-ins out of wave D, and here that is learnt at the end of the plan, too late to use the room.

Two kinds of risk in one plan: the first paired device, then screen control. It fits (20 h and 40 steps by my count), but the deny list is Gateway-wide, so the two entries lifted for the pilot are lifted for the phone that was paired days earlier in the same plan, and the plan rests on re-reading the phone's command list at that point. The deps proposal shows the split is possible at the cost of one more exit gate.

In two waves the piece named to give way is not the last build phase. In G the group chat (phase 3) is built before 'email me this' (phase 4, the least certain phase, with T5's send-tool turn); in H printing (phase 2) is built before switching (phase 3). An overrun in the last phase cannot be relieved by moving a phase that is already built.

Exit tests that stop short of the goal, in two places. Wave A: only Tony asks 'did I get an email about X?', although the goal says either parent can. Wave C: only the planted flyer that must set nothing is run; no real flyer is turned into reminders after a yes.

Over one plan by its own count (25.25 h and 51 steps; 25.75 h and 51 by mine) and left undecided: 'if that is read as over one plan, Jordan's inbox opens wave B'. Wave B has no room for it: B is 24 h by my count and about 26.25 h with her inbox and her lookup checks, so the overflow starts a chain (see wave D).

Four plans in a row sit at the ceiling (my count: A 25.75 h, B 24 h, C 24.25 h, D 23.5 h) and all the room is in E to H, after the plans that hold the untried tests. The give-way chain does not close. Jordan's inbox into B pushes the day out into C (26 h); C pushes the flyer dates into D (24.5 h); C's stated second piece, the rest of the reminder work (about 5 hours), would make D about 29.5 h, and D's only named give-way (the clash watch, 3.5 h) still leaves it at 26 h. Eight waves leave an average of under 3 hours of room a plan, and it is in the wrong half.

T1's day-8 search is listed in phase 5 (its tests list is T1), after the reader phase (phase 4, tests T2 only) that is built on the token. Phase 4 says only that it starts on or after day 8 'by default' and lets Tony start sooner at the cost of about 3 hours redone, so the test sits after what relies on it. In the same wave the sign-in check (phase 6) goes live after the 07:00 schedule is switched on (phase 5), the other way round from what the check is for.

The phase order puts the largest and least certain block last. The paper cards, photos and hourly weather are built first; then come the outbound gate (7.5 h, with its night in report mode), the helper and the day between the two parents' agents. So the fixed waits fall at the tail instead of running beside other work, the firewall is switched to blocking every program with attachments and both mail texts already live, and the second piece named to give way (hourly weather, phase 3) is already built when an overrun in the gate shows. The planted-file test is run twice and the second run is not counted. As in the risk proposal, the paper cards come after the first unattended texts.

The clash watch is the first no-model command job the jobs script creates in this proposal, and no phase names the check that the script can create a command job (the command-job part of T3, which the sizing file puts on the page watch) or that a command job can use the stored calendar sign-in. The other two proposals name the first of these where their first command job is built.
The send-to-owner test's injected web page is run in wave E, before the browser exists. Wave F adds the browser and does not run that test again through it.

Two kinds of risk in one plan, and what gives way has nowhere to go: 'a short plan of its own', which is an unplanned ninth wave. The same Gateway-wide deny-list point applies as in the risk proposal's last wave.

Exit tests that stop short of the goal. Wave A: only Tony asks 'did I get an email about X?'. Wave C: only the planted flyer that must set nothing is run. Waves D, F and G: every scheduled job is hand-started (the monthly cover text, the clash check, the page watch, the weekly text and the 'still on' check), so no run is seen arriving by itself and no schedule line is proven.

graft.what: Wave C, phase 1 'Try it first: T5 and T7', before any rule is written. Both results are then known at the start of the plan: a failed T7 frees about 6 hours early, and a T5 that shows the check is not called for connector tools is put to Tony before the calendar phase. It replaces T7's late place in the risk proposal's phase 6.

Get-ready phases that ask at the start for the details that take a parent time to gather: the school district's calendar, the facts for the family pages and a short label for each of the two children (the shared pages and logs wave); the page or feed to watch, the pages the plain reader could not read and one video or podcast link (the watcher and harder-reading waves). Each is still listed under tony_provides and none holds the wave.

The decisions a test result can ask of Tony, listed under tony_provides in the wave where the test runs: a failed day-8 search, a failed T4, T5 not called for connector tools, a failed T6, a failed T7, and his signature if his own agent can quote the 07:00 text.

Wave A's give-way rule in full: the decision point is when Tony's 07:00 text and the sign-in check are live; if the plan is over by then, the lookup is built for Tony alone and Jordan's inbox opens wave B; until then Tony's school lines cover the school mail that both parents receive. Add the matching form of the exit test for that case, which the risk proposal lacks.

The note that the jobs script holds eight or more scheduled jobs by the house wave, and that S9's comparing step has no hours in any wave. Put a check of the job count, and of what T3 showed about a job added twice, into the get-ready phase of the wave that adds the three watcher jobs.

T8 and the two paper pages (1.5 h) may be done inside wave A's eight-day wait when the first week runs ahead of its 8.5 hours, as the deps proposal draws them and the use proposal's notes allow; otherwise they stay counted in wave B. That puts Jordan's half page in her hands before her 07:00 text starts where there is time for it.

The go-live check for the house-rules plugin in wave C: besides a text, a weather question and a mail lookup, both 07:00 mail texts still arrive the next morning, because the scheduled path also runs through the new blocking check.

Optional, if one kind of risk per plan is wanted at the end: the split of the last wave after the deny list, with the phone app as one light plan and the screen-control pilot alone in the last. By my count that is about 10 h and 14 h in place of one plan of 20 h, at the cost of one more exit gate.
